title: The metadata Version row reads 2 while the file family reads v3
source: Recovery Workbench Definition of Ready and Done v3
section: Metadata table rows Version and Date; file name
description: The metadata table reads Version 2 and Date 28 October 2026, while the file name of the same document reads v3. Version 4 takes the next family version under Template and Rules R8.2 and keeps both source readings word for word, so a reader sees Version 2, Date 28 October 2026 and Family version of this copy 4 in one table.
evidence: Metadata table: Version 2, Date 28 October 2026. File name: Recovery Workbench Definition of Ready and Done v3.docx. Template and Rules R8.2: the next version is the highest v<n> of the family plus 1.
proposed: Confirm the version number of the family and whether the metadata row should follow the file name; keep the source reading until the document owner rules.

title: No owner per service is stated, and no owner table exists
source: Recovery Workbench Definition of Ready and Done v3; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
section: Section 1 Checked by column; section 5 Who owns each definition
description: Version 3 states owners as roles and team types only, in the Checked by column of section 1 and in section 5, and it never names a service for a story, a table, an endpoint, an event, a workflow or a job. Version 4 adds table 1.1 with the 19 services of Architecture v5, their wave, schema and REST base from the Ownership Map v1, and the suggested owner team of R5.3, and it makes the owning service an item of the definition of ready (section 2.3, item 24).
evidence: Section 1 Checked by: Analyst with the tech lead and QA, Tech lead, Reviewer, Product owner, QA lead, Business lead, Release owner with the application owner. Section 5: four definitions, each owned by a role or a team type. Ownership Map v1 sheet Services: 19 rows with code, service, wave, schema, REST base, topic and queue.
proposed: Confirm table 1.1 as the owner reference of every story and keep the roles of section 1 and section 5 for the gate approval itself.

title: The definition of ready does not require a published contract
source: Recovery Workbench Definition of Ready and Done v3; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
description: Version 3 asks the story to state the trigger, the service, the events published, the idempotency key and any call out of the module, and it does not require the contract to be published, versioned or faked before the story is pulled. Version 4 keeps item 8 and adds section 2.3, items 21 to 25: contract published in the Service Contract Catalog v1, fake published, version fixed, ownership stated, Ready to start.
evidence: Section 2.1 item 8, one cell of text, naming no contract document, no version and no fake. Architecture v5 slide 11: every service publishes its contracts (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, activity jar) before code; contract tests run in every build. Template and Rules R5.4: a class C dependency builds against the published contract and its fake.
proposed: Confirm the five items of section 2.3 as mandatory for every story that consumes or provides a contract, and confirm the Service Contract Catalog v1 as the place the contract is published.

title: The definition of done names no boundary test and no contract test result
source: Recovery Workbench Definition of Ready and Done v3; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Section 3.1 item 2 Pipeline; section 3.2 item 12 Boundaries; new section 3.5
description: Version 3 lists contract tests inside the nine pipeline gates and requires the story to touch one module, and it never makes a boundary test a result of its own nor says what the boundary is once the monolith is split. Version 4 keeps both items, reads one module as one service and one schema, and adds section 3.5, items 21 to 27: contract tests green, boundary test green, event compatibility, replay test, decision record test, version published, fake retired.
evidence: Section 3.1 item 2: build and unit tests, lint, secret scan, PDPA lint, container scan, module boundary, integration and contract tests, AI first-pass review and human approval. Section 3.2 item 12: the story touches one module, or the other module's code owner has approved. Architecture v5 slide 29: boundary test fails on a cross-schema reference. Architecture v5 slide 46: contract tests per API, event and activity, Temporal replay tests, Testcontainers.
proposed: Confirm the seven items of section 3.5 as the results that decide Done, and confirm that the module boundary gate of item 2 is the same gate as the boundary test.

title: No contract version, compatibility or withdrawal rule is stated
source: Recovery Workbench Definition of Ready and Done v3; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: New section 2.3 item 23; section 3.5 items 23 and 26
description: Version 3 names no contract version, no compatibility rule and no way to withdraw a contract or a fake. Version 4 requires the story to state the version it builds against, reads a later change as a new version with BACKWARD compatibility in the JSON Schema registry, and makes a breaking change a new contract with its own story. How long a version or a fake stays published is not stated in any source read.
evidence: Version 3: the words version, compatibility and deprecated appear nowhere in sections 1 to 5. Architecture v5 slide 11: OpenAPI 3.1 with /v1 in the path; AsyncAPI 3.0 with a JSON Schema registry, backward compatible; the activity interface in a contract jar. No source read states a withdrawal period or a deprecation window.
proposed: Confirm the version and compatibility rule as written and decide the withdrawal period of a contract version and of its fake.

title: One module means the monolith module in the source and a service and schema after the split
source: Recovery Workbench Definition of Ready and Done v3; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: Section 1 Plan approved row; section 3.2 item 12 Boundaries
description: Two source rows use module as the unit a plan and a story may touch: the plan touches one module, and the story touches one module or the other module's code owner approves. After D-RCV-60 the unit is the service and its schema rwb_<short>, and the owner is the team of the Ownership Map v1. Version 4 reads module as service and schema and keeps the wording of both rows otherwise unchanged.
evidence: Section 1 row Plan approved: the plan names every file, test and migration and touches one module. Section 3.2 item 12: the story touches one module, or the other module's code owner has approved. Architecture v5 slide 29: one schema per service, no cross-schema joins or keys, a boundary test in every build. Ownership Map v1: 19 services and 19 schemas.
proposed: Confirm that one module is read as one service and its schema from this version on.

title: A tracker record is named in the definition of done while tracker work is out of scope
source: Recovery Workbench Definition of Ready and Done v3; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 R1 U6
description: The source row is labelled with the name of the issue tracker and requires the pull request to carry the story key. D-RCV-60 makes no tracker access or update and holds tracker impacts in one separate file, so version 4 relabels the row Tracker, keeps the pull request and merged commit requirement, and points at the separate impact and follow-up file without naming a tracker record.
evidence: Section 3.3 row 18: label Jira, text the pull request carries the story key, and the story records the merged commits. Template and Rules R1 U6: no issue-tracker access or updates; tracker impacts go to one separate file only. Template and Rules R8.3: Issue-tracker impact and follow-up v1 sits in folder 22.
proposed: Confirm the relabelled row and confirm that no tracker record is written in this document.

title: Integration stories and class I dependencies are not covered by either definition
source: Recovery Workbench Definition of Ready and Done v3; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
description: The source predates the integration epics RWB-ITG-W1 to RWB-ITG-W4 and the class I dependency, so neither definition says what makes an integration story ready or done, nor how the harness story RWB-ITG-W1J01-ITG is judged. Version 4 adds a note to section 5.1: an integration story carries the same ready and done items, and it alone may carry class I dependencies.
evidence: Template and Rules R5.1: RWB-ITG-W1 to RWB-ITG-W4 and RWB-ITG-NFR. R5.4: class I is the real cross-service behaviour, allowed only on ITG stories. Section 2 and section 3 of the source name no integration story and no class I dependency.
proposed: Confirm that an integration story uses the same two definitions and that the harness story is judged by section 3.5 like any other story.

title: No owner and no approval path are stated for contract publication or for the boundary test
source: Recovery Workbench Definition of Ready and Done v3; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 R5.3
description: Section 5 names an owner and a change path for the definition of ready and the definition of done only. Contract publication and the boundary test are new conditions of version 4 and have no owner and no change path in the source. Version 4 adds two rows: the owning service team from its contract story, changed only by a new published version after a four-eyes review, and the owning service team with the DevOps team on the golden pipeline, changed only with platform approval.
evidence: Section 5: two rows, Definition of ready and Definition of done, each with an owner and a Changed by cell. Template and Rules R5.3: CON and APP work is TechX (suggested); OPS work is the DevOps team (suggested). Template and Rules R5.7: a CON story is always Day 1. No source read states who approves a contract version.
owner_role: Product owner; service owner; DevOps lead
proposed: Confirm the two added rows and the four-eyes review path for a contract version.

title: The worked example is a monolith story key with no service and no realignment equivalent
source: Recovery Workbench Definition of Ready and Done v3; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
description: The worked example of a story that meets the definition of ready is RWB-E1-020, allocate a new case to a queue and an owner, a key of the monolith story set with no service and no contract. Version 4 keeps the example word for word and adds the contract story RWB-P3-E1042-CON, parameters, as the example that shows every item of section 2 including the published contract.
evidence: Section 1, last paragraph: The worked example of a story that meets the definition of ready is RWB-E1-020, allocate a new case to a queue and an owner. Template and Rules R5.2: story keys follow RWB-<scope>-<legacy compact>-<work type>. R5.5 DP-06: parameters are H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and C RWB-P3-E1042-CON. Ownership Map v1 sheet Parameters: parameters P3, rwb-case contract RWB-P3-E1042-CON.
proposed: Confirm the added example and confirm whether a microservice worked example replaces RWB-E1-020 or stands beside it.
